Colorado Springs is a space town, but is it a NAS 410 town? SNT-TC-1A and NAS 410 for local NDT technicians

Colorado Springs carries the Space Force's name on its bases, yet most of the large defense and space employers here do engineering, software and operations rather than build flight hardware. Northrop Grumman's local teams work on missile defense and the Sentinel program. Boeing staff run ground systems for the WGS satellite constellation. L3Harris teams operate Space Force systems at Schriever Space Force Base, and the Aerospace Corporation runs a Space Warfighting Center in the city. Peterson and Schriever Space Force Bases, Cheyenne Mountain, the Air Force Academy and Fort Carson complete the picture. Very little of that puts a penetrant line or an ultrasonic flaw detector in a technician's hands, so the NAS 410 question in the Springs is narrower than the skyline suggests. It comes up in specific places.

The shops that do touch flight hardware

Precision machining, welding, composite and finishing shops along the I-25 corridor make parts for space and defense primes, many of whom build their spacecraft and launch hardware an hour north around Denver. Those customers write the NDT personnel requirement into the purchase order, commonly NAS 410, and it flows down to whichever sub-tier runs the inspection. A shop with that clause needs a Responsible Level 3 designated in writing, a written practice that meets the standard's minimums, formal documented training, and records a Nadcap AC7114 or customer auditor can follow from a signed report to the inspector's file. Defense work has carried this habit since NAS 410 replaced MIL-STD-410.

Military maintenance on the installations

Army aviation and ground equipment at Fort Carson, and aircraft maintained on the Air Force and Space Force installations, are inspected by service members working under each service's own technical orders and personnel rules, which sit outside both civilian schemes. Contractors who support those units follow their contract; defense contracts frequently name NAS 410, but some name a service-specific requirement, so ask which one yours cites.

Pueblo steel, utilities and construction on SNT-TC-1A

Pueblo's steel mill, the utilities' power plants and transmission structures, Cripple Creek mining and highway and building steel along I-25 buy UT, MT, PT and VT to AWS D1.1, ASME and owner specifications. Contractors on that work certify under written practices built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A. For many Springs technicians that is the steadier employment, with an aerospace supplier job as a later move rather than a first one.

Making the move from utility work to an aerospace supplier

  1. Ask the supplier which standard and revision its written practice follows. NAS 410 Revision 6 was released in December 2025, and customers set when shops adopt it.
  2. Ask who the Responsible Level 3 is, and request a review of your records before your start date.
  3. Expect certification to start again. An SNT-TC-1A certificate is useful evidence, but by itself it does not fulfill a NAS 410 requirement.
  4. Allow time for formal penetrant and magnetic particle training, the surface methods where NAS 410 asks for more than SNT-TC-1A recommends.
  5. Keep course outlines with hours, a signed experience log per method, examination records marked with their standard, and a yearly vision record. Military spouses who move often should keep their own copies, since the file is what follows them.

Atlantis for Colorado Springs

Atlantis training is built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A: self-paced online theory with Q&A from our ASNT NDT Level III (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT), practice in the Practical NDT simulator, and the hands-on practical at your employer's facility. There is no Atlantis classroom in Colorado Springs. Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3 to employers in the Pikes Peak region. A supplier's RL3 decides whether outside coursework counts toward its NAS 410 certifications; settle that before you enroll. Suppliers can use aerospace written practices built on SNT-TC-1A and NAS 410 audit documentation support, prepared for their RL3's approval. For the comparison, read NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A; for programs built on the ASNT document, see SNT-TC-1A for aerospace NDT. The space primes themselves are covered on NDT training in Denver.
